mainTopic: What a מקרא teacher is really paid for (רב: watching; רבי יוחנן: verse breaks and טעמים), and how this explains the משנה about vows and a ברייתא about learning on שבת.
overview: The משנה said that a person forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend may learn מדרש from him but not מקרא. The גמרא explains that pay is allowed for teaching מקרא but never for מדרש, so only a free מקרא lesson counts as a real gift. Two פסוקים in דברים teach that Torah must be taught for free. That raises the question of why מקרא may be paid for at all. רב says the teacher is paid for watching the children, and רבי יוחנן says he is paid for teaching the verse breaks and the טעמים. The גמרא challenges רב, since an adult needs no watching. It answers that the משנה is talking about a child, and that the משנה is missing words: a child may not be taught, but an adult and his sons may. Next, a ברייתא saying children may review on שבת but not learn new verses seems to fit only רבי יוחנן. The גמרא pushes back that pay for שבת is allowed when it is included in a weekly wage. It then starts quoting a ברייתא about hired watchmen to prove this, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pay is allowed for teaching Bible but not for teaching מדרש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that even where teachers are paid, pay is allowed only for מקרא and not for מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that even in a place where people take payment for teaching, it is allowed to take pay for teaching מקרא, but it is not allowed to take pay for teaching מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה lets the man teach מדרש but not מקרא to someone who may not benefit from him. The difference is about whether teachers may be paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching מקרא is a paid service in this place, so a free lesson saves the student money, and that counts as forbidden benefit. Teaching מדרש may never be paid for, so teaching it free gives no extra benefit. That is why it stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
The written text of the Torah and תנ"ך (Bible)
Explaining the Torah: its laws and דרשות

phrases.english: This teaches us
that even in a place where they take payment
for teaching Bible it is permitted to take payment
for teaching מדרש it is not permitted to take payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an earlier question (before this section) about the משנה's split between מדרש and מקרא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a new distinction: pay is allowed for מקרא but forbidden for מדרש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think מקרא and מדרש should be treated the same for a person under a vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Free מקרא lessons are a real benefit because they are normally paid for, while free מדרש lessons are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole sugya: why one kind of Torah teaching may be paid for and the other may not.

steps.title: Why may one not take pay for מדרש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes מדרש different, so that teachers may not be paid for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about מדרש, that one may not take payment for teaching it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source and reason behind the rule that teaching מדרש must be free. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 stated the rule without a reason. Here the גמרא wants to know where the 'no pay for מדרש' rule comes from.

phrases.english: What is different about מדרש, that one may not take payment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that one may not be paid for teaching מדרש.

steps.title: Torah must be taught for free, learned from פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: From two פסוקים in דברים, the גמרא learns that Torah must be taught for free, just as it was taught for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the Lord commanded me at that time to teach you,' and it is written: 'See, I have taught you statutes and laws as the Lord commanded me.' Just as I did it for free, so too you must do it for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with פסוקים showing that Torah teaching was given for free. So we too must teach it for free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים connect משה's teaching to ה׳'s command. The lesson is that Torah teaching is meant to be free, the same way it was given. This is the source for not taking pay for מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (a פסוק is coming)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And the Lord commanded me at that time
to teach you"
and it is written: "See, I have taught you
statutes and laws, as the Lord commanded me"
just as I did it for free
so too you must also do it for free.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים teach that Torah must be taught for free, just as it was taught for free.

steps.title: Then Bible should also be taught for free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוקים are about all Torah teaching, so מקרא should also have to be free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bible too should be taught for free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If Torah must be taught for free, why may a teacher be paid for מקרא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'teach for free' source does not seem to split between מקרא and מדרש. So the distinction from step 1 now looks baseless. The גמרא needs to explain what the מקרא teacher is actually being paid for.

phrases.english: Bible too should be taught for free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from step 3 to attack the distinction from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 1 that pay is allowed for teaching מקרא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים require all Torah teaching to be free, and מקרא is Torah too.

steps.title: רב: the teacher is paid for watching the children
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a Bible teacher is not paid for the Torah itself but for watching over the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The payment is for watching the children.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the מקרא teacher's pay is really for babysitting the young students. It is not payment for teaching Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since children learn מקרא, the teacher also has to supervise them, and that work may be paid for. The Torah teaching itself stays free, so the rule from the פסוקים is kept.

phrases.english: Rav said:
It is payment for watching.
phrases.notes: The teacher is paid for supervising the kids, not for the Torah he teaches.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the payment is for.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pay for מקרא seemed to be payment for teaching Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pay is for watching the children, so the Torah itself is still taught for free.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the teacher is paid for teaching how to read the verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers differently: the teacher is paid for teaching where verses break and how to read them with the טעמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The payment is for teaching the breaks in the verses and the טעמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer to the same challenge. The pay is for teaching how to read and punctuate the verses with the טעמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the reading skill (breaking up verses and the musical notes) is a separate service that may be paid for. This is part of teaching מקרא, but it is not the Torah teaching that must be free.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking up the verses and reading them with the טעמים (cantillation notes)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is payment for teaching the punctuation of the verses with the cantillation notes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: שְׂכַר פִּיסּוּק טְעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4, disagreeing with רב in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the payment is for, in a different way than רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pay for מקרא seemed to be payment for teaching Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pay is for teaching punctuation and the טעמים, which is a separate service.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: an adult does not need watching
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's rule 'he may not teach him מקרא', the גמרא challenges רב, since an adult needs no watching.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: He may not teach him מקרא. This works well for the one who says the pay is for teaching the breaks and the טעמים, because that is why he may not teach him. But for the one who says the pay is for watching, does an adult need watching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both answers against the משנה. רבי יוחנן's view fits well, but רב's view seems to have a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pay is for the reading skill, a free lesson saves even an adult money, so the משנה's ban makes sense. If the pay is only for watching, an adult needs no watching, so a free lesson gives him no benefit. Then why does the משנה forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted this view works ... but the other view is difficult
According to the one who says

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה: He may not teach him Bible.
Granted, according to the one who says
it is payment for punctuation with cantillation notes
this is why he may not teach him
but according to the one who says it is payment for watching
is an adult someone who needs watching?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answers of steps 5 and 6 against the משנה and attacks רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that the pay is for watching (step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An adult under the vow needs no watching, so a free lesson would give him no benefit, yet the משנה forbids it.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about a child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב: the משנה is speaking about a child who is under the vow, and a child does need watching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching about a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב by saying the משנה is about a young child. A child needs supervision, so free lessons would give him real benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the student was an adult. By placing the משנה's case with a child, the watching is a real paid service. Teaching him for free would be forbidden benefit, so רב's view fits the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: A מקרא teacher may be paid, not for the Torah itself, but for watching the children (רב) or for teaching the breaks and טעמים (רבי יוחנן). מדרש must always be taught for free. רב explains the משנה as talking about a child, who needs watching.

phrases.english: It is teaching about a minor.
phrases.notes: He means the person under the vow is a young child, who does need supervising.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רב in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה's case to a specific situation (a child).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be talking about an adult, who needs no watching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a child, who needs watching, so free lessons are real benefit even according to רב.

steps.title: A child does not have sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer that the משנה is about a child, because the end of the משנה talks about teaching 'his sons.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה is about a child, look at the end of the משנה: 'But he may teach his sons מקרא.' Does a child have sons?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8 by reading the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the משנה's ban on teaching מקרא is about a child, who needs watching. But the end of the משנה lets him teach 'his sons,' which only makes sense for an adult. So the משנה seems to be talking about an adult after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child who is not yet an adult
Look at the end part of the same משנה

phrases.english: If it is about a minor,
say the end part of the משנה:
'But he may teach his sons מקרא.'
Is a minor someone who has sons?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the defense of רב given in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is talking about a child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה mentions the person's sons, which only fits an adult.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words: a child may not be taught, but an adult and his sons may be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: He may not teach him מקרא when he is a child. If he was an adult, he may teach him and his sons מקרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in missing words in the משנה so that both parts fit רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה has two cases. A child needs watching, so teaching him for free would be a gift of free babysitting, which is forbidden. An adult needs no watching, so teaching him is pure Torah and is allowed. The 'sons' clause belongs to this adult case, which solves the problem from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words, and the גמרא fills them in
And this is what it is teaching

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the ban on teaching מקרא applies to a child, because a child needs watching; an adult and his sons may be taught.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
'He may not teach him מקרא' is about a minor;
if he was an adult,
he may teach him and his sons מקרא.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading missing words into the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה talks about one person, so mentioning sons means he is an adult.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה has two cases: a child may not be taught; an adult and his sons may be taught.

steps.title: Children do not learn new material on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that children do not start new verses on שבת but may review, which fits רבי יוחנן but seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Children may not read a new passage for the first time on שבת, but they may review what they already learned. This works for the one who says the pay is for teaching verse breaks and טעמים: that is why they don't read new material on שבת. But for the one who says the pay is for watching, why can't they read new material on שבת, and why can they review? Either way there is pay for watching on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a new challenge against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting paid for work on שבת is a problem. For רבי יוחנן, new material means new teaching of verse breaks and טעמים, which is paid work, while review needs no new teaching. For רב the teacher is paid for watching, and he watches the children whether they learn new or old material, so the ברייתא's difference makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, usually from a ברייתא
For the first time, new material
It works well for... (one view, but not the other)

phrases.english: They challenged from a ברייתא:
Children may not read a passage for the first time on שבת,
but they may review what they learned before.
It works well for the one who says
the pay is for teaching verse breaks and טעמים:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן from Step 6.

phrases.english: that is why they do not read for the first time on שבת.
But for the one who says the pay is for watching,
why may they not read for the first time on שבת,
and why may they review?
Either way there is pay for watching on שבת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the teacher is paid for watching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Watching happens with both new and old material, so רב cannot explain why the ברייתא treats them differently.

steps.title: Even רבי יוחנן's pay is allowed when included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even pay for teaching verse breaks is not forbidden on שבת, since it is included in the weekly wage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, is pay for teaching verse breaks on שבת forbidden? It is included in the weekly pay, and included pay is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge by showing it was built on a wrong assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that pay for teaching new verses on שבת is forbidden. But the teacher is paid for a whole week, so the שבת part is just 'swallowed into' the larger wage, and that is allowed. So the ברייתא's reason cannot be about forbidden pay at all, and it proves nothing against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
Pay for שבת that is included in a larger wage

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying it is fine to be paid directly for שבת work. Only pay that is part of a weekly or longer wage is allowed.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
is pay for teaching verse breaks on שבת forbidden?
It is included in the larger wage,
and included pay is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge in Step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The premise that the ברייתא is about forbidden שבת pay
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Pay for teaching on שבת is part of the weekly wage, so it is not forbidden even for רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא about hired watchmen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins bringing a ברייתא about workers hired to watch, to prove that included שבת pay is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who hires a worker to watch a child, to watch a cow, or to guard seeds does not give him pay for שבת. Therefore...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא as proof that included pay is allowed; the quote continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a worker hired by the day may not be paid for שבת itself. The word 'therefore' sets up the rest of the ברייתא, which will show how pay that is included in a longer wage works.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Pay for the day of שבת

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֵל לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת הַתִּינוֹק,
phrases.english: One who hires a worker to watch a child,
to watch a cow,
or to guard seeds —
does not give him pay for שבת.
Therefore...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the claim in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: That pay included in a larger wage is permitted on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about workers hired to watch a child, a cow, or seeds
